criterion_scores.reasoning: ALLOW allowlists match market-intel-schema.sql exactly for company/topic/event/event_entity and correctly excludes person.email per ADR-9; phone/email regexes pass all 18 selftest cases including the documented separator/+ tradeoff for phone. But req() (line 213) exposes a public guard_writes kwarg that, when a caller passes guard_writes=False directly, skips guard_body entirely — this directly contradicts the module docstring's own claim (line 6) 'There is no in-run override' and the PRD's ratified decision 'guard is automatic, not opt-in.' Internally write() only uses this safely (it pre-guards before disabling), but the escape hatch is importable and documented as a general entry point.

AC1 fully covered (selftest exercises email/phone/nested-metadata/denylist/unknown-table/non-allowlisted-column cases, positive and negative). AC2's check_writers() has two real detection gaps: the .mjs/.js branch only matches urlopen|requests.(post|patch|put)|curl — no fetch(/axios pattern at all, despite explicitly scanning JS files. The .md prose regex alternates only on topic|event|company|person|event_entity, omitting documents|doc_chunks|doc_claims (all present in ALLOW). No self-test exercises the req(..., guard_writes=False) bypass path either.

Correct file placement, REST-not-MCP (BASE matches market-intel-spine.md's canonical ref), .env loading pattern matches the worktree convention, table-sync comment correctly cross-references the schema files, and the (status, parsed_json) / prefer= / timeout=60-for-dockb conventions from the six migrated writers are preserved as documented. Docked for the guard_writes opt-out breaking the explicit 'not opt-in' convention set by the PRD's own decision log.

No hardcoded secrets (key loaded from .env/env var at runtime), no orphan metrics, no tombstoned-decision resurrection. But exposing a working, documented guard_writes=False override on req() reintroduces the exact shape of the 'advisory guard' alternative the PRD explicitly rejected. A hard-fail security chokepoint should not ship with a callable disable switch on its own public function.

Error messages are excellent and match spec exactly (field · tier rule · fix), and selftest/check-writers output is legible. But the module docstring's factual claim 'There is no in-run override' is contradicted by the code's own guard_writes parameter — the dishonest-framing failure mode the rubric's diagnostics anchor calls out, applied to the code's own documented contract.

top_fixes: Remove or privatize the guard_writes kwarg on req() — let write()'s pre-guard and req()'s guard both run (guard() is pure/cheap).
Add a fetch(/axios detection pattern to check_writers()'s .mjs/.js branch.
Extend the .md prose-detection regex to include documents|doc_chunks|doc_claims.
